page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-128 is a memory-dense compute instance provisioned on the x86_64 architecture. The instance runs on AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources consist of 8 physical cores mapped to 16 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Processing cores are provisioned with dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding resource contention from noisy neighbors.

The hardware configuration includes zero GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage, meaning that operational persistence and file system volumes must be attached via remote block storage. Network provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system offers high memory density relative to its processing footprint. This allocation profile suits memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large relational database systems, in-memory key-value stores, distributed caching layers, and memory-constrained analytical data pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-128 is a memory-dense virtual server featuring 16 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9J45 x86_64 processors running at 2.7 GHz, providing 8 physical cores with two threads per core. With an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, the instance maintains a high memory-to-core ratio suited for data-heavy execution. The configuration excludes local storage disks and GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent volumes. Network connectivity provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. Due to the high memory capacity and dedicated compute cores, this instance profile is designed for in-memory databases, caching tiers, data analytics, and enterprise backend applications requiring substantial RAM headroom.
